headline: Eurozone Inflation Hits Three-Year High of 4% in October on Energy Costs
summary: Eurozone inflation climbed to a three-year high of 4.0 percent in October. Official data showed the surge was driven by rising energy costs resulting from the Middle East war.
why: Higher inflation erodes consumer purchasing power and complicates monetary policy decisions for the European Central Bank, directly impacting bond yields and currency valuations.

impacts.name: Eurozone Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
impacts.why: Official data confirms Eurozone inflation reached 4.0 percent in October.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Higher-than-expected inflation data typically forces markets to reprice interest rate expectations, influencing bond yields and currency values.
